item.description:
Moscow, Russia — Novaya Gazeta staff hold up portraits of slain journalists as they hold a last editorial meeting before the newspaper shuts down, citing what it described as a relentless campaign by the authorities, in Moscow. On 29 October, two things became known: Novaya was being evicted from its newsroom, and banks would stop processing readers’ donations to Novaya (its only legal income). Insiders spoke of the risk of Novaya being declared an extremist organisation – then any employee could be jailed: a journalist, an editor, an accountant or a cleaner. — Photograph: Ramil Sitdikov/Reuters

Source: The Guardian — Photos of the Day

Netanyahu’s far-right coalition lost its majority in the election after four years in power. The main Jewish opposition bloc also fell short, however, leaving two Arab Israeli parties, the Joint List and Ra’am, holding the balance of power. — Photograph: Ilia Yefimovich/AFP/Getty Images
